name: Luke S. Johnson
role: Missionary and member of the first Quorum of the Twelve
dateNote: Section 68 was given to him and others on 1 November 1831; he became an apostle in February 1835.
importance: Luke Johnson, a son of John Johnson of Hiram, was baptized in May 1831 and sent to preach in section 68. Section 75 pairs him with William E. McLellin, and section 102 lists him on the high council. He was one of the first Twelve Apostles from 1835 until he broke with Joseph Smith in late 1837. He was excommunicated in 1838, rebaptized in 1846, and went west in 1847.
connections: His father John Johnson and brother Lyman E. Johnson also appear in the D&C. Orson Hyde, his brother-in-law, rebaptized him.

sources.title: Luke Johnson, Joseph Smith Papers biography

reviewNote: Career checked on JSP. JSP gives no death date; Wikipedia gives 9 Dec. 1861 in Salt Lake City. The text names him only as “Luke Johnson,” never with the middle initial.
